title: You can find the biggest
idea: Review-heavy close of the max unit; consolidate and hint that the smallest uses the same pattern flipped.

exercises.prompt: In one sentence, how do you find the biggest value in a list?
options: Keep a best-so-far starting at the first value, and replace it whenever you meet something bigger
exercises.explanation: That is the whole max pattern: a best-so-far you replace on a bigger value.
42 is the largest. best climbs to 42 and nothing beats it.

exercises.prompt: To find the SMALLEST, you would keep a 'best so far' too — but replace when you meet something SMALLER.
exercises.explanation: A sneak peek at the next unit: smallest is the SAME pattern as biggest, just flipped. You'll change one comparison.

exercises.prompt: If max uses 'if n > best', what comparison would 'find the smallest' likely use?
exercises.explanation: Flip > to < and the same loop finds the smallest. Next unit makes this exact move.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: put the max program in order one more time.
exercises.explanation: Start best, loop, test with >, replace on a win, print. You know this now.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: 'add up all the donations' uses which tool?
exercises.explanation: 'Add up all' is the running-total sum pattern from Unit 57.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: 'how many donations were over 100' uses which tool?
exercises.explanation: 'How many fit a rule' is the counter-with-if from Unit 58.

exercises.prompt: Which statements about max are true? (pick all)
options: Start best at the first value
Replace best when you meet something bigger
Start best at 0 for any list
exercises.explanation: First two are the correct pattern. Starting at 0 breaks on negatives, and adding is sum, not max.
All equal to -1, so the biggest is -1. Starting at the first value handles all-negative lists.

exercises.prompt: You finished the max unit. What is the big takeaway?
options: A best-so-far that you replace on a bigger value finds the biggest — and flipping the test finds the smallest
Max is unrelated to everything else
Only sorted lists have a biggest
exercises.explanation: Best-so-far is the core idea, and it flips cleanly to the smallest. That transfer is exactly next unit's point.
